input: Schedule a chimney sweep before the first fire

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing when the user plans to have their first fire sets a hard deadline for booking the appointment — if it's weeks away vs. days away, urgency changes dramatically.
Whether this is a wood-burning fireplace, gas insert, pellet stove, or wood stove affects what type of sweep service is needed and which companies to contact.
The user may only want a cleaning, or they may also need an inspection, liner check, or cap repair — this changes what to ask for when calling companies.
Whether the user wants help finding a certified sweep or already has a company in mind determines the very first action to take.
If a landlord, property manager, or HOA is involved, the user may need approval or coordination before booking, adding steps to the plan.
The user may have priorities like lowest cost, fastest availability, CSIA-certified technicians, or strong reviews — this shapes which companies to shortlist.
Knowing what 'done' looks like — a booked appointment, a completed sweep, or a written inspection report in hand — determines where the task ends.

gold.taskTitle: Schedule chimney sweep before first fire of season
gold.taskDescription: Arrange a professional chimney sweep appointment in time to safely use the fireplace for the first time this season.

questions.title: When do you plan to have your first fire?
questions.description: The target date for the first fire sets the booking deadline and determines how urgently the appointment needs to be made.

questions.title: What type of fireplace or stove do you have?
questions.description: Wood-burning fireplace, gas insert, pellet stove, or wood stove each require a different type of sweep service.

questions.title: Do you need only a cleaning or also an inspection?
questions.description: Clarifies whether to book a standard sweep or a more thorough Level 1/Level 2 inspection with the sweep.

questions.title: Do you already have a sweep company in mind?
questions.description: Determines whether the first action is researching and shortlisting companies or simply calling a known provider to book.

questions.title: Is anyone else's approval needed before you book?
questions.description: A landlord, property manager, or HOA may need to be involved or notified before scheduling a service visit.

questions.title: What matters most — lowest price, fastest slot, or certification?
questions.description: Knowing the user's priority helps narrow down which companies to contact first when comparing options.

questions.title: What does done look like — appointment booked or sweep completed?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the task ends at securing a booking confirmation or only once the actual sweep has been carried out.
